To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have used the recent released Plancks data, including both temperature power spectrum and the lensing potential power spectra, to constrain two modified gravity models: $f(R)$ model and chameleon-type model in the Berstchiger-Zukin paramatrization.

we have constrained modified gravity using Planck data and found that the data favor a relatively higher value of Hubble constant and a relatively small Compton wavelength for the extra scalar degree freedom.
the modified gravity parameters are constrained by the Planck CMB data, especially by the small-scale CMB lensing data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the constraints on $f(R)$ modified gravity and chameleon-type gravity using Planck CMB data.
the modified gravity constraints using the latest released Planck data and other data sets.
how well the modified gravity can be constrained with the current CMB, BAO, $H_0$, supernovae data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Planck data can give a tight bound on the Compton wavelength for the $f(R)$ model, while for the chameleon model, the data set we used can only provide a tight constraint on $\beta_1$ but cannot constrain $B_0$.
, with Planck CMB data alone we cannot exclude modified gravity as the underlying theory, and the Planck lens power spectrum data is the key to improve the bound on the modified gravity parameters.
the current observational data can not constrain the modified gravity models, but can give an upper bound on $B_0$.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Planck has provided the tightest constraints on modified gravity models to date, especially on the chameleon-type one.
the modified gravity models we studied are still consistent with the Planck data, although the constraints from the Planck data are much stronger than those from the WMAP data.
, with the help of the lensing potential power spectra data from Planck, the constraints on modified gravity models can be significantly improved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Planck lensed temperature power-spectrum and lensing potential data are crucial for constraining the modified gravity parameter.
Planck CMB lensing power spectrum data are crucial for constraining modified gravity models.
the Planck lensed CMB power spectrum can give very tight constraint on the modified-gravity parameters, which can help to distinguish between modified-gravity models and LCDM model.
